primarySources.title: OpenProcess
primarySources.meaning: OpenProcess accepts an exact PID and desired access; false inheritance is explicit. Failure is NULL and requires immediate error capture.

primarySources.title: GetProcessTimes
primarySources.meaning: A successful BOOL validates creation and all-thread kernel/user counters from the same process handle. CPU counters use 100-nanosecond units; success zero is valid and aggregate CPU may exceed elapsed wall time.

primarySources.title: GetLastError
primarySources.meaning: Save an API failure error immediately before later calls can overwrite it. Successful calls do not make stale error values a failure.

primarySources.title: CloseHandle
primarySources.meaning: Close each real successfully opened process handle exactly once; preserve failure. Closing a handle does not terminate its process.

primarySources.title: FILETIME
primarySources.meaning: Combine high and low DWORD fields as unsigned 64-bit. Calendar FILETIME uses a 1601 UTC epoch and 100-nanosecond units; the format does not promise measurement resolution.

primarySources.title: Process security and access rights
primarySources.meaning: PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION (0x1000) is sufficient for GetProcessTimes; no all-access or privilege elevation is needed.

methodContract.whitelist: Only id/type pairs copied from the owned browser CDP SystemInfo.getProcessInfo response. No Get-Process/GetProcessById/EnumProcesses or wider OS process enumeration.
methodContract.nativeCallsPerWhitelistedPid: One OpenProcess, one same-handle GetProcessTimes after successful open, one CloseHandle in finally after successful open.
methodContract.validity: Native BOOL success flags and null success error fields are required. API failure, invalid/missing schema or evidence, changed source/request bytes, PID/type or creation identity changes, counter reset, nonfinite derived values and incomplete process sets retain null canonical totals.
methodContract.filetimeEncoding: Unsigned uint64 decimal strings, compared exactly for creation identity. Kernel and user ticks are subtracted using BigInt separately before summing and converting to CPU seconds.
methodContract.successZero: A true Win32 successful query with zero user/kernel counters is measured zero. Chromium CDP cumulative zero remains ambiguous and is never upgraded without actual Win32 successful reads.
methodContract.unitAndResolution: CPU tick unit is 100 nanoseconds. Neither FILETIME shape nor units imply 100ns measurement resolution.
methodContract.window: Both arms use the same two boundary protocols, before tracing/collection to after closed raw measurement window and before tail cleanup. The driver supplies its actual shared monotonic wall interval, never the literal formal duration as denominator.
methodContract.chronology: The before endpoint must end no later than the after endpoint starts. Individual start/end brackets must also be finite, nonnegative and ordered.

boundedExecution.executable: Caller-pinned absolute powershell.exe or pwsh.exe; no installed version/path assumed by this report.
boundedExecution.timeoutMeaning: 5000ms triggers stopping, not an absolute receipt deadline. Existing runner may add taskkill timeout 2500ms plus close proof wait 3000ms.
boundedExecution.stopping: Forced timeout/cancel/output-cap requires confirmed owned process-tree stop for helperLeaseReleasable. Ordinary closed helper reports direct_process with tree status null; no machine lease or unrelated browser cleanup is asserted.
boundedExecution.requestIntegrity: Create a new wx bounded JSON request; retain exact bytes/path and before/after hashes. The pure summarizer independently requires the after hash to equal the original raw-request hash.
boundedExecution.sourceIntegrity: Hash the fixed helper and selected executable before and after the child; paired endpoints require the same paths and source hashes. Preserve output SHA and actual monotonic brackets.
boundedExecution.failure: Policy blocks, API errors, child failure, output limit, timeout or missing stop proof are preserved. No bypass or fallback enumeration.

limits: This is cumulative all-thread CPU for the typed CDP-owned endpoint PID sets, not renderer-only, audio callback, DSP, hardware underrun, hearing or product GUI evidence.

Matching two endpoint PID/type/creation sets does not prove no transient processes existed between them. A CDP list and a later Win32 open remain sequential observations; CDP supplies no creation epoch to close that initial ownership race.

PowerShell cold start/Add-Type compilation/IPC and sampling skew have cost. This method records helper duration and boundaries; it does not measure external helper/Node CPU or assert zero instrumentation overhead.
Readings are per-process sequential calls, not an atomic machine snapshot. Ratios may exceed one on multiple threads/cores.
Native failures remain unknown. A successful unit fixture cannot establish installed PowerShell/.NET version, Win32 availability, actual hardware rate or native CPU values.

No source proof or unit result adopts formal qualification, overwrites prior failures, changes original V3/frozen44 sources, lowers workload/voice/path/geometry/capture caps, relaxes numeric/core/50ms gates or replaces a real 600-second measurement.
The original CDP-only source method report 18 is historical and unchanged. Old audio-runner zero assumptions are not retroactively corrected into native evidence.
